body.purpose: Ledes, bios, case copy in Manrope.

headline.purpose: Section headlines with grape/lime emphasis words.

label.purpose: Eyebrows, nav, stickers, counters in uppercase DM Mono.

dos: Do crown one candy accent per section and let typography carry the rest (One-Accent-Per-Section Rule).
Do set display type in Bricolage 700-800 with tight tracking; keep body in Manrope and labels in DM Mono (Three-Voice Rule).
Do pair every shadow with an ink border and >=12px radius (Sticker-Stock Rule).
Do animate only transform and opacity with the spring curve; gate hover motion to fine pointers and kill movement under reduced motion.
Do label proposal-stage numbers as proposals, never results - proof over promises.
Do end every page one click from an inquiry.
donts: Don't use gray minimalism, timid hairlines, or interchangeable geometric sans headlines - the confirmed anti-reference.
Don't put two candy fills in competition on one screen, and don't set muted text on candy fills.
Don't invent testimonials, metrics, pricing, or social profiles the company has not provided.
Don't add shadows without borders, animate layout properties, or ship motion without reduced-motion handling.
Don't flatten toward restraint by merely shrinking everything - remove shadows and let type do the work (per the Restraint Direction).
keyCharacteristics: Warm paper canvas with deep plum ink; never pure black on pure white.
One accent per section; accents never compete on the same screen.
Editorial type scale: giant display, confident headlines, quiet mono labels.
Tactile surfaces: 1.5-2px ink borders with hard offset shadows.
Motion is springy and spatial: blur-and-rise entrances, staggered groups, zero layout-property animation.
narrative.overview: Dun Digital reads like the sunniest newsstand on the street: warm paper, oversized editorial headlines you can read from across the road, and color used the way a good newsstand uses covers - to earn the glance, then let typography and hierarchy do the selling. Every surface leads with a massive Bricolage Grotesque statement, supports it with plain-spoken Manrope copy, and stamps it with small mono labels that feel printed, not rendered. The system is expressive but disciplined: one dominant accent per section, generous whitespace (88-110px section rhythm), and recurring signature devices - sticker pills with hard offset shadows, lime marker highlights behind key words, and a tilted ink marquee band.

rules.body: Each section crowns exactly one dominant candy accent for grounds, shadows, and headline emphasis. Micro-accents (10px chips, numerals, caption flags, alternating card shadows) may rotate through the family - they read as confetti, not competition. If two accents ever share the same visual weight on one screen, delete one.
rules.name: The One-Accent-Per-Section Rule

rules.body: Marigold, lime, and bubblegum backgrounds always carry plum-ink text; grape and tangerine fills may carry white or paper text. Never place muted mauve text on a candy fill.
rules.name: The Ink-Text-on-Candy Rule

rules.body: A screen may speak in Bricolage (statements), Manrope (explanations), and DM Mono (labels) - never a fourth voice, never Bricolage for body copy.
rules.name: The Three-Voice Rule

rules.body: Lime marker highlights are reserved for the single most important phrase per hero; headline emphasis inside sections uses flat grape/lime color, not markers.
rules.name: The Marker Rule

rules.body: If a surface has a shadow, it also has an ink border and a radius of 12px or more - shadows never float on bare rectangles.
rules.name: The Sticker-Stock Rule

rules.body: The system currently sits at its maximum tactile weight. Future refinement should remove shadows before adding any: prefer flat cards with stronger typography over more pop.
rules.name: The Restraint Direction
